Date of Encounter: 2024-09-19Care Plan:PPARG (sensitivity to fat in diet, obesity, insulin resistance):Omega-3 Fatty Acids (EPA/DHA): 1–3 g/day to improve insulin sensitivity and inflammation.Monounsaturated Fatty Acids (MUFA): Incorporate olive oil, avocado, and nuts.Berberine: 500 mg 2–3 times/day to help manage blood sugar levels.2. TCF7L2 (insulin resistance, obesity):Magnesium: 300–400 mg/day to enhance insulin sensitivity.Chromium Picolinate: 200–400 mcg/day to help with glucose regulation.Alpha-Lipoic Acid: 300–600 mg/day as an antioxidant and insulin-sensitizer.3. SLC2A2 (higher intake of sweets):Inositol (myo-inositol): 2–4 g/day to improve insulin sensitivity and reduce sugar cravings.Chromium Picolinate: 200–400 mcg/day to reduce sugar cravings.4. FTO (higher BMI, body fat in sedentary individuals):Vitamin D: 1000–2000 IU/day to support metabolism and weight regulation.Green Tea Extract (EGCG): 300–500 mg/day to help with weight management.Coenzyme Q10: 100–200 mg/day to support energy production and metabolism.5. IRS1 (G>A) (insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes):Magnesium: 300–400 mg/day to improve insulin sensitivity.Resveratrol: 100–250 mg/day to support glucose metabolism.Fiber (Psyllium or glucomannan): 5–10 g/day to improve glycemic control.6. MTHFD1, MTR, MTRR (homocysteine metabolism):Methylated B vitamins (B12 and Folate): 1000 mcg/day of Methylcobalamin (B12) and 800 mcg/day of Methylfolate to support homocysteine metabolism.Choline: 550 mg/day to counteract deficiencies and support methylation.Trimethylglycine (TMG): 500–1000 mg/day for methylation support.7. COMT (methylation, B vitamin metabolism):Magnesium: 300–400 mg/day to support COMT function.Methylated B vitamins: Ensure adequate intake of B6, B12, and Folate (see dosages above).8. GSTM1 deletion, GSTP1 (detoxification, oxidative stress):N-acetylcysteine (NAC): 600–1200 mg/day to boost glutathione production.Sulforaphane (from broccoli extract): 50–100 mg/day to support Phase II detox.Curcumin: 500–1000 mg/day for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects.9. eNOS (reduced nitric oxide, risk of atherosclerosis):L-arginine: 3–6 g/day to enhance nitric oxide production.Beetroot extract: 500 mg–1 g/day for nitric oxide support.CoQ10: 100–200 mg/day for cardiovascular health.10. MnSOD/SOD2 (oxidative stress):Selenium: 100–200 mcg/day to support antioxidant enzymes.Vitamin C: 500–1000 mg/day as an antioxidant.Alpha-Lipoic Acid: 300–600 mg/day to reduce oxidative stress.11. IL-1, IL-6, CRP (inflammation):Omega-3 Fatty Acids (EPA/DHA): 1–3 g/day to reduce inflammation.Curcumin: 500–1000 mg/day for anti-inflammatory support.Resveratrol: 100–250 mg/day to modulate inflammatory pathways.12. VDR BSM1, VDR Taq1 (bone density, Vitamin D metabolism):Vitamin D: 1000–5000 IU/day depending on levels.Calcium: 1000 mg/day to support bone health.Magnesium: 300–400 mg/day to support bone density.Vitamin K2: 100 mcg/day to direct calcium to bones.13. CYP2R1, GC variants (Vitamin D metabolism):Vitamin D: 2000–5000 IU/day to compensate for reduced conversion.Magnesium: 300–400 mg/day for better Vitamin D utilization.14. FADS1 (increased inflammation from Omega-6):Omega-3 Fatty Acids (EPA/DHA): 1–3 g/day to balance Omega-6 intake.Avoid seed oils: Focus on healthy fats like olive oil and reduce Omega-6 fatty acids.15. HLA DQ2.2/DQ2.5 (celiac disease risk):Gluten-free diet: Eliminate gluten from the diet.Probiotics: To support gut health, especially if gluten has been ingested.16. AGT (heterozygous) (hypertension risk):Magnesium: 300–400 mg/day to support blood pressure regulation.Coenzyme Q10: 100–200 mg/day for cardiovascular health.Reduce salt intake: Keep dietary salt to a minimum.These supplements and dietary recommendations aim to mitigate the risks associated with these specific SNPs by addressing metabolic, cardiovascular, inflammatory, and detoxification pathways. Regular monitoring and adjustment of doses based on individual responses and lab work are
